self_check.spec_coverage: Went through every test bullet in the 41.3 spec (todo.md at 0d28e02) and each one has a matching test in test_crm_send.py: new visitor, same occurred_at when the clocks straddle a second, touch vs begin after a lapse, found by BSUID, number beats BSUID, key -> agent_reply -> handover_changed order, no console_reply, history and audit source/tool row, duplicate / 502 / 504 change nothing, the fault-isolation cases, the shared console takeover (D8), events switched off. I ran the spec's three mutations on a git-archive copy of d9cb7d8 in my scratchpad, never in the worktree. M1: _tell_crm without occurred_at turns the cross-second test red. M2: agent_reply queued after the takeover turns the order test red, plus one more. M3: _file re-reading the record turns only test_a_takeover_that_fails_still_files_the_reply red, and only by accident: the re-read returns None for a record that was never saved. That is a weakness in the mutation, not in the code. crm_send is the only thing holding this record object during the call, and begin() has already saved, so re-reading in order loses nothing. The two-copies hazard that the spec's rationale points at only shows up with a concurrent writer, and no test in the suite covers that (see e2e). Where a test fakes a failure (user_store.get raising RuntimeError, handover.begin raising, the audit store raising) it tests the developer's own try/except rather than a failure that happens for real: the real user_store.get falls back to memory and does not raise for an input that has passed validation. That is fine for fault isolation, but those tests do not show that such a failure can actually occur.

phase2.rebuttals: Most of the self-defence holds, and I checked it rather than taking it on trust. (a) The suite numbers: they report 1304 passed with CRM_EMAIL/CRM_PASSWORD set. I got 2 failed / 1302 passed through the shared entry point, and the 2 also fail on base. That matches their own note from 41.2 that red and green do not mean the same thing on both sides for this suite. It is not a defect of this task, but it is a standing hole in the review contract, and it is still open. (b) The mutation for '4.4 re-reads the record': the spec says that re-reading the record and then writing turns a history or takeover test red. Read literally, a re-read inside _file after the takeover, it does not: 167 passed and 1 failed, and the 1 fails only because the re-read returns None for a record that was never saved. The developer quietly chose a stronger version, writing to a copy read before the takeover, which gave 8 failed. That copy is the real hazard, so the defence holds on substance. But what the record claims ('4.4 改成重新读档案再写 → 历史或接管测试变红') is true only for their version, not for the spec's literal wording. In sequential flow a re-read is harmless; the two-copies danger needs a second writer at the same time, and no test has one. (c) Self-decision 4, 'reading the record failed, so return without a takeover; building a blank one would overwrite the real record once Redis recovers': the conclusion is fine, but the reason does not fit the branch. The real user_store.get never raises when Redis is down; it silently falls back to memory and returns None. So the case they worry about is the normal path: get_or_create builds a blank record in memory, the takeover and history go there, and once Redis is back the bot reads the real record, which has no takeover. The spec already accepts this ('发送后 user_store 退回内存……同一种降级'). The except branch they defend is reachable only through a bug or a mock. (d) Rollout step 1 says the public URL should give 'not 503'. I probed production: POST https://chatbot.acuventech.com/internal/crm/send -> 405 text/html, and POST /internal/whatsapp/inbound -> 405 text/html. That second route does exist on the deployed backend; if the edge forwarded it, the answer would be the backend's JSON, not nginx HTML. So the edge nginx does not forward /internal/ today, which backs up the claim 41.1 only read from config. The rollout step could say '期望 405 text/html' instead of 'not 503'; a stricter expectation would catch a forward that answers with something other than 503. 41.1 is not deployed yet: origin/master is still 270fa7d. (e) Self-decisions 1-3 (begin_for before save, START and END spans after the send, input.to = key_id) all hold.
phase2.blind_spot: The developer flagged nothing that I missed outright; their record has no defect they admit and I failed to see. Two things they wrote that I did not test in phase 1: the extra mutations (begin-only without touch; _file not swallowing exceptions; audit source written as 'human'), which back up the coverage claim beyond the spec's three, and the note about LF/CRLF after mutating. I ran into the same CRLF trap in my own mutation script: two of three patterns failed to match at first. My review would have gone wrong silently if I had not printed 'pattern not found'. A mutation that never applies reads like a mutation that was caught. The blind spot this shows: in phase 1 I checked the spec's mutations only as worded, and did not ask which form of each mutation reproduces the hazard the spec cares about. The developer did ask that for 4.4. I also accepted the fault-isolation tests as they are, and only in phase 2 did I follow through that the case they defend (Redis down) never reaches their except branch.
